items.quote:
if
				not Recommendations.CanAct(current)
				or not before
				or not now
items.what: `not before` and `not now` are unreachable: both are guaranteed non-nil when the preceding CanAct checks pass
items.why: At the call site, `Recommendations.CanAct(item)` is checked first (line 140): it calls `ValidPlace(item.step or (item.aside and item.aside.place))`, so when it returns true, `before = item.step or item.aside and item.aside.place` is non-nil. Inside the loop, `not Recommendations.CanAct(current)` is tested before `not now`; if CanAct(current) is true, `current.step or (current.aside and current.aside.place)` is valid, so `now` is non-nil. No spec exercises either branch: tests with no-step/no-aside items are caught by the outer CanAct guard. This is the Unreachable-guards anti-pattern.
items.reason: Removing not before and not now produces six LuaLS need-check-nil diagnostics in Act coordinate comparisons. The guards narrow the optional place types, matching the defensive-noise exclusion for type checks.

items.quote: seconds = seconds + math.max(0, objective.need - (objective.have or 0)) * 4

items.why: Both size the same thing, how long a step's work takes, one for lap worth and one for the session budget. Differences: Laps scales by WorkFactor for above-level quests and counts max(1, need); Session counts need minus have and returns nil for explore or unknown counts. Those look intentional (different questions), but the per-count and per-talk seconds are the same tuning values and Session's are unnamed, so retuning Laps leaves the session estimate behind.

What remains is one bare `* 4`, the Settled 'One-line idioms' shape and the lens's small-idiom exclusion; an unnamed number is not a second implementation.

items.what: A journey's zone or instance ID is recovered by pattern-matching its key string at every read site instead of being a typed field Model sets once; add the ID to AGFJourney (or one Model accessor) and read that.

The key is a persisted identity (prefs.journey), which is a wire format, but it is not converted once at a boundary: types/Namespace.lua AGFJourney has no zone or instance field, so each consumer carries its own copy of the pattern. A typo in one pattern, or a new key prefix, is not found by LuaLS or luacheck; the mismatch silently yields nil (no dungeon page entry, wrong moment text, zone left out of Completion).

items.quote:
Overview.HubLine = HubLine
Overview.DropLine = DropLine
Overview.Progress = Progress
items.what: Overview hands out the pieces of a card's third line and footer (DropLine, HubLine, Progress, Stops) and each caller reassembles them in the same order: UI/Panel.lua:792 and UI/WindowJourneys.lua:248 for a whole card, UI/Panel.lua:1054-1057 and UI/WindowJourneys.lua:269-273 for a compact or grid card.

CardTooltip (Overview.lua:394-400) then has to guess which of those lines the card showed (`card.detail == hub`, `card.state == "compact"`). The precedence rule (log-full note, then reason, then hub, then subline) is the thing Overview's header says panel and window must never disagree on, and it lives in the callers; the reason line and the footer/progress pair would move behind Overview.
items.reason: The shallow-modules exclusion for a caller needing the pieces apart applies: UI/WindowJourneys.lua:254-263 uses Progress independently for the featured footer, hiding it without progress, while grid cards fall back to Stops. Overview.CardTooltip also uses HubLine independently, so the exported pieces serve varying compositions despite the repeated detail precedence.

items.what: card.ShowButton is fully dead; remove the stored alias and its field annotation, keeping the button itself.
items.why: Whole-repository searches, including tests, tools, hidden configuration, workflows, docs, XML, generated data and available host annotations, find only this assignment and the annotation at line 32. items.quote: card.journey, card.state = journey, "shown"

Panel supplies "chosen" for the active journey. Overview.CardClick uses that state to refocus an already-running journey without calling ns.Choose, or resume it when paused; "shown" instead calls ns.Choose(key, titleStartsRoute). With the default titleStartsRoute=true, Core.lua:712 and 791-792 restart guidance through StartRoute. A read-only stdin LuaJIT reproduction using tests/harness.lua, spf="v1+", completed={844}, and log quests 845 (complete) and 843 selected the route and then clicked its visible window card: route.chosen=true, card.state="shown", ns.Choose called once, and NavigateRoute increased 1 -> 2. The window intentionally keeps the large-card layout, but that visual choice should not change the shared click/tooltip contract. Found while comparing the parallel map/window implementations; fixing this changes behavior and is not a cleanup-only edit.

items.what: A stock recipe is a bare 4-tuple whose meaning lives only in this comment, and its one caller module unpacks it by index in four places: tools/screenshots.py:133-134 (`recipe[1]` as the size function), :139-141 (`recipe[2]`, turning (point, x, y) triples into anchor dicts against the parent), :190-192 (`recipe[3]` as a raised-frame flag) and :215-219 (`recipe[0]`, with `if recipe[0] is draw_scroll_frame` to pass that one recipe a fifth argument). tools/screenshots_test.py:103 unpacks it a fifth way (`(draw, *_)`).

Adding a field or a second recipe needing the child height means editing every index site and the identity check in screenshots.py, a file with 23 commits in the last three months. Named fields and a uniform draw call would sit behind the interface; where the seam goes is a design choice.
items.reason: The cited sites are real, but the lens asks for complexity that reappears in each caller, and here there is one caller module (tools/screenshots.py) that reads each slot at exactly one site: size in intrinsic(), anchors in defaults(), frameLevel and draw in Layout.frame(), with the test only taking slot 0. Nothing is repeated, so moving it behind the recipe relocates the four reads rather than removing any, and the claim that a new field means editing every index site is wrong since indices 0 to 3 and `(draw, *_)` survive an appended field; the `recipe[0] is draw_scroll_frame` special case is a single-site wart, not caller-repeated work.
